description: Why traditional networks are hard to change and how separating the control plane from the data plane fixes that: OpenFlow, SDN controllers and network applications, network function virtualisation, programmable data planes with P4, and SDN in data centres and operator networks. Every idea is built and tested on emulated networks of virtual switches, with students writing controller applications and data-plane programs that run against live traffic.
modelledOn: Open Networking Foundation, OpenFlow Switch Specification
Goransson, Black and Culver, Software Defined Networks: A Comprehensive Approach
Nadeau and Gray, SDN: Software Defined Networks
ETSI Network Functions Virtualisation (NFV) architectural framework
outcomes: Explain the limits of distributed, vendor-closed networks and how SDN separates the control and data planes.
Program OpenFlow switches with flow tables, match fields, actions and counters to implement forwarding and filtering.
Build network applications on an SDN controller, such as a learning switch, a load balancer and a firewall.
Design virtualised network functions and service chains and explain the NFV management and orchestration stack.
Write P4 programs for a programmable data plane and reason about their parsing, match-action and pipeline behaviour.
Evaluate SDN deployments in data centres, wide-area networks and mobile operators for scalability, reliability and security.

units.title: Limits of traditional networks
topics: The traditional router and switch: integrated control and data planes, vendor-specific operating systems and command-line configuration
Distributed control: routing protocols, spanning tree, convergence and the difficulty of enforcing global policy
Operational pain: manual configuration, misconfiguration outages, slow feature rollout and middlebox sprawl
Early programmability: active networks, ForCES, the 4D project and Ethane as precursors to SDN
Setting up the emulator: virtual hosts, Open vSwitch and a scripted topology

units.title: Control and data planes
topics: Data plane, control plane and management plane: responsibilities and timescales
The SDN architecture: logically centralised control, southbound and northbound interfaces, the network operating system
Physical versus logical centralisation; controller placement and the consistency-availability trade-off
Abstractions for forwarding, distribution and specification; the network as a graph the controller computes on
Network virtualisation: overlays, tunnelling with VXLAN and GRE, network hypervisors and slicing

units.title: OpenFlow
topics: OpenFlow switch model: flow tables, match fields, priorities, actions, instructions, counters and timeouts
Multiple tables and pipelines, group tables (all, select, fast failover) and meter tables
The OpenFlow channel: hello, features, packet-in, packet-out, flow-mod, barrier and port-status messages
Reactive versus proactive flow installation; table-miss handling and flow-table capacity limits
Capturing and decoding OpenFlow messages; installing flows by hand from the command line
Alternatives and complements: NETCONF and YANG, OVSDB, gNMI

units.title: SDN controllers
topics: Controller architecture: event loop, topology discovery with LLDP, host tracking, device and flow databases
Open-source controllers compared: Ryu, ONOS, OpenDaylight; distributed controllers and clustering
Northbound interfaces: REST APIs, intent-based networking and policy languages
Controller scalability and fault tolerance: state replication, leader election, switch-to-controller failover
Consistent network updates: two-phase updates, race conditions and transient loops

units.title: Network applications on the controller
topics: A learning switch and shortest-path routing written as controller applications
A stateless firewall and access control driven by a policy file
A server load balancer and traffic engineering from link utilisation statistics
Monitoring: polling flow counters, sampling with sFlow and detecting heavy hitters
Testing and verifying applications: header space analysis and checking for loops and black holes

units.title: Network function virtualisation
topics: From hardware middleboxes to virtual network functions: firewalls, NAT, load balancers, deep packet inspection
The ETSI NFV framework: NFV infrastructure, virtual network functions, management and orchestration (MANO)
Service function chaining and steering traffic through chains with SDN
Performance of software packet processing: kernel bypass, DPDK, SR-IOV and smart NICs
Containers and cloud-native network functions; orchestration with OpenStack and Kubernetes
Building a chain of a virtual firewall and NAT in the emulator and measuring its throughput

units.title: Programmable data planes
topics: Why fixed-function switches are limiting: the protocol-independent switch architecture
The P4 language: headers, parsers, match-action tables, actions, control blocks and deparsers
Targets: software switches, programmable switch ASICs and smart NICs; the P4Runtime control interface
In-band network telemetry and other data-plane applications (load balancing, caching, congestion signalling)
Writing and testing a P4 program for a custom header on a software switch

units.title: SDN in data centres and wide-area networks
topics: Data centre fabrics: leaf-spine and Clos topologies, ECMP, overlays and multi-tenant virtual networks
SDN for cloud providers: tenant isolation, virtual routers and the host virtual switch
Software-defined WAN: centrally engineered inter-data-centre traffic and SD-WAN for enterprise branch offices
Internet exchange points and software-defined exchanges; keeping traffic local at African IXPs

units.title: SDN in operators, security and capstone
topics: SDN and NFV in mobile operators: virtualised packet core, control and user plane separation in 4G and 5G, network slicing
Transport SDN and segment routing for operator backbones
Security of SDN: the controller as a single target, flow-table exhaustion, securing the control channel, SDN for DDoS mitigation
Capstone: an emulated campus or operator network with a controller application for routing, access control and monitoring, plus one P4 or NFV extension

schedule.title: Limits of traditional networks
schedule.exercise: Describe a real misconfiguration outage in a traditional network, explain which part of the integrated control and data plane design made it hard to prevent, and list what an early programmable approach like Ethane changed.

tasks.title: Configure a three-router chain with static routes from the CLI and note how many separate device configurations a single path change touches
Fail a link in a ring of routers running a routing protocol and record the convergence time and the interim loss of packets
Build a scripted topology of three virtual hosts and two Open vSwitch switches, verify reachability, and export the topology as a rebuildable script

schedule.title: SDN architecture and planes
schedule.exercise: Draw the SDN layers with southbound and northbound interfaces, then argue how many controllers a four-site African operator needs, weighing latency against consistency.

tasks.title: Label each function of a given switch (forwarding, routing computation, SSH access) as data, control or management plane and test each by disabling it
Connect three OpenFlow switches to one controller in the simulator and verify the controller discovers all switches and their ports
Place one controller in a four-site topology to minimise worst-case switch-to-controller latency, and compare with a two-controller placement

schedule.title: Abstractions and network virtualisation
schedule.exercise: Explain how a controller turns a topology graph into forwarding rules, and describe how VXLAN lets two tenants share a physical network with overlapping addresses.

tasks.title: Compute the shortest path between two hosts on a given topology graph in Python and list the switch hops a controller would program
Create a VXLAN or GRE tunnel between two virtual switches and verify two hosts on different physical subnets share one logical segment
Create two tenant virtual networks with overlapping 10.0.0.0/24 ranges on the cloud console and prove that traffic stays isolated between them

schedule.title: OpenFlow switches and messages
schedule.exercise: For five packets, decide which flow entry matches in a given flow table with priorities and write the resulting action and the counter values after the packets pass.

tasks.title: Install one flow entry matching a destination MAC and outputting to a port, send three pings, and read the packet counters in the flow table
Build a two-table pipeline where the first table filters by VLAN and the second forwards, and verify with test packets that each stage acts
Configure a fast-failover group with primary and backup ports, break the primary link, and show traffic switches over without a controller call

schedule.title: Flow installation and management protocols
schedule.exercise: Compare reactive and proactive flow installation for a 500-host campus on first-packet delay and table size, and write the NETCONF XML to read an interface configuration.

tasks.title: Use the switch command line to add, list and delete three flow entries by hand, and verify the packet path changes after each step
Compare reactive and proactive installation by measuring first-packet delay for 10 new flows and counting packet-in messages for each
Fill the flow table to capacity with generated flows, observe the table-full behaviour, and add idle timeouts that keep the table within limits

schedule.title: Controller architecture and northbound interfaces
schedule.exercise: Compare Ryu, ONOS and OpenDaylight on language, clustering and typical use, and sketch the REST calls an operator app would make to request a path between two hosts.

tasks.title: Watch LLDP discovery on a four-switch topology and list the links the controller finds in the topology database after startup
Write a script calling a controller REST API to list switches and install a flow, then verify the flow in the switch table
Write a small controller event handler in Python that logs host arrivals, tracks host locations, and updates when a host moves ports

schedule.title: Scalability, failure and consistent updates
schedule.exercise: Explain how three controller replicas keep state consistent when one fails, and show with a diagram how an uncoordinated update can create a transient forwarding loop.

tasks.title: Stop the primary controller in a two-controller setup and verify switches fail over and hosts keep reaching each other
Step through a leader election among five controller nodes after the leader fails, and record the term and votes at each step
Update a path across four switches in the wrong order to cause a transient loop, then redo it using a two-phase update that avoids it

schedule.title: Writing SDN applications
schedule.exercise: Design a controller application with policy file input that routes by shortest path, blocks listed hosts, and balances two servers, then specify how you would verify it.

tasks.title: Complete a learning switch controller app, then ping between four hosts and verify it installs flows only after learning the MAC addresses
Write a firewall app that reads a policy file of allowed host pairs and verify that blocked pairs fail and allowed pairs succeed
Write a checker that analyses installed flow rules for loops and black holes and run it on a topology with two planted faults

schedule.title: Network function virtualisation
schedule.exercise: Map the ETSI NFV blocks to a virtual firewall deployment, and design a service chain that sends web traffic through firewall then cache while other traffic bypasses it.

tasks.title: Replace a hardware firewall in a diagram of a small office with a virtual firewall on a host and confirm the same traffic is permitted and blocked
Steer only HTTP traffic through a virtual firewall using flow rules and verify other protocols take the direct path
Deploy a virtual network function on the cloud console behind a load balancer, scale it to three instances, and verify traffic is distributed

schedule.title: Performance and building chains
schedule.exercise: Compare kernel packet processing and DPDK on a 10 Gbit/s link for per-packet cost, and write a plan to containerise a firewall and NAT function with orchestration.

tasks.title: Measure throughput between two hosts on a software switch at three packet sizes and record how small packets reduce the rate
Build a service chain of a virtual firewall then NAT between a LAN and server, and verify addresses are translated and blocked ports fail
Deploy a containerised NAT function on a managed cluster, autoscale it under generated load, and report throughput before and after scaling

schedule.title: Programmable data planes with P4
schedule.exercise: Write the parser, match-action table and deparser for a custom header with a 16-bit tag field in P4, and explain how P4Runtime would populate its table.

tasks.title: Read a given P4 program and write down its header definitions, parser states and match-action table keys in a summary table
Add a custom header with a 16-bit tag to a P4 program on a software switch and show packets are forwarded according to the tag
Write a P4 program that records per-packet queue depth into a header and reports the maximum seen for each hop in a test run

schedule.title: Data centres, WANs and exchanges
schedule.exercise: Design a leaf-spine fabric for 200 servers with ECMP, estimate oversubscription, and explain how a software-defined exchange in Accra could keep local traffic local.

tasks.title: Build a two-spine four-leaf topology and verify that every pair of leaves has two equal-cost paths by tracing packets
Steer traffic between two sites over the cheaper or faster link according to a policy and verify the path changes when the link fails
Build a software-defined exchange with three networks, install policy-based peering rules, and show local traffic never leaves the exchange

schedule.title: Mobile networks, security and capstone
schedule.exercise: Prepare a design report for an emulated campus network with a controller application for routing, access control and monitoring, plus one P4 or NFV extension, with a threat analysis of the controller.

tasks.title: Separate a mobile core into control and user plane nodes in the simulator and verify a handset session passes through the user plane node
Flood a switch's flow table with random flows to show exhaustion, then add a defence that limits flow installs per host and re-test
Build an emulated campus with a controller app for routing, ACL and monitoring, verify with a test plan, and add one NFV service
